newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish coalition loses absolute majority.
newsitem.headline: Turkish coalition loses absolute majority.

text.p: A Turkish MP announced his resignation from the coalition True Path Party on Friday, costing the Islamist-led government its absolute majority in parliament.

True Path deputy Yildirim Aktuna, a former health minister in the government, handed out copies of his resignation letter at a news conference and said he would give it to conservative True Path leader Tansu Ciller later in the day.

The resignation takes the number of MPs in Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's beleaguered government to 275, one less than the absolute majority needed to win any vote of confidence at the 550-member assembly.
But Erbakan still has a simple majority of two over the secularist opposition.
The government has slowly been falling apart since the powerful army began pushing it in February to crack down on Islamist activism.
Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader, was to meet Ciller later on Friday for talks on possible early elections.
